day1_lunch_start.text: *Fourth period is over and the lunch bell rings. Students get up all at once.*

choices: Sea asked me to eat with her, so I stay in the classroom
My head hurts. Try the nurse's office
Eat lunch alone on the rooftop

day1_lunch_sea_1.text: *Sea pushes two desks together and pulls a lunchbox out of her bag.*

day1_lunch_sea_2.text: Two tiers? You can't eat all that alone.

day1_lunch_sea_3.text: Is this all yours? You haven't even opened it yet, but it looks like a lot. You want to show off more now that I'm watching, don't you?

day1_lunch_sea_4.text: Well? Good enough to sell, right?

day1_lunch_sea_5.text: *She opens the lid. Rolled omelet, mini sausages, rice balls, broccoli, cherry tomatoes. Each item has its own compartment.*

day1_lunch_sea_6.text: Wait. Did you make all of this yourself? I thought you were just sharing leftovers, but this must have taken work. Can I really have some?

day1_lunch_sea_7.text: Have some. If you only eat bread, you'll be hungry again by afternoon.

day1_lunch_sea_8.text:
*Sea picks up a piece of rolled omelet with her chopsticks and holds it out.*

Oh, I can take it myself.

day1_lunch_sea_9.text: Here, try the omelet first. I made it on the sweet side.

day1_lunch_sea_10.text:
*The rolled omelet is still warm. The sweetness comes through first.*

You really did make it sweet. Still warm too.

day1_lunch_sea_13.text:
*Sea stopped with her chopsticks raised, then smiled a beat late.*

Why are you smiling? I mean it. It's really good. You eat some too.

day1_lunch_sea_14.text:
*During a brief lull in the conversation, Sea nudges the lunchbox dividers into place with the tips of her chopsticks.*

Have some more. There's plenty left.

day1_lunch_sea_15.text: Do you always bring a lunchbox like this, Sea?

day1_lunch_sea_16.text: Yeah. School lunch is fine, but homemade food tastes better.

day1_lunch_sea_17.text: It's a little much to eat alone.

day1_lunch_sea_18.text:
*Sea's chopsticks stop above an empty compartment of the lunchbox.*

It's almost empty. Sorry, I ate it all. You should have been the one telling me to slow down.

day1_lunch_sea_19.text: *Sea pauses for a moment, then smiles.*

day1_lunch_sea_20.text: I made a lot today. I'm glad you're eating it.

day1_lunch_sea_21.text:
*The lunchbox is almost empty. There's some time left.*

There's still time. Thanks for the lunch. Tell me something else too.

day1_lunch_sea_23.text: *Sea hands me one of her earbuds. A mellow guitar track.*

day1_lunch_sea_24.text: Oh, what's this? The guitar's so soft, I didn't realize it had started. We can talk over it without any trouble.

day1_lunch_sea_25.text: I've been listening to it a lot lately. I like that it doesn't have lyrics.

day1_lunch_sea_26.text:
*We share the earphones.*

I like the guitar. I could listen to this for a while.

day1_lunch_sea_27.text: Not bad. I can see why you play it so often.

day1_lunch_sea_28.text: I don't usually talk about things like this.

day1_lunch_sea_29.text:
*We talk about music, then YouTube. The earbud cord lies loosely across the middle of the desk, and lunch is almost over.*

Lunch is nearly over already. Give me the earbud; I'll wind up the cord. If you're still thinking about the song in class, ask me its title.

day1_lunch_yuna_1.text: *I enter the library. It's quiet, probably because everyone is at lunch.*

day1_lunch_yuna_2.text: *I was about to sit in a corner seat when I heard a 'click.'*

day1_lunch_yuna_3.text: *A girl holding a camera freezes, startled. She's tiny beside the oversized camera.*

day1_lunch_yuna_4.text: Did you just take my picture? I heard the shutter as I came in. Tell me straight away if you caught me pulling a weird face.

day1_lunch_yuna_5.text: Oh, no. I'm in the photography club. I was taking pictures of the light by the window when you came in...

day1_lunch_yuna_6.text: I'm sorry. I'll delete it right away.

day1_lunch_yuna_7.text: No, it's fine. You're in the photography club. You lowered your camera as soon as you saw me; I thought I'd startled you.

day1_lunch_yuna_8.text: Yes. I'm Choi Yuna, a first-year. You're the transfer student, right?

day1_lunch_yuna_9.text: Yeah. I'm {name}. Nice to meet you.

day1_lunch_yuna_10.text:
*Yuna cups the camera in both hands and lowers her head.*

You really care about that camera. If you hold it like that, I feel like I'm snooping. I won't touch it.

day1_lunch_yuna_11.text: Do you come to the library often? I'm here every day.

day1_lunch_yuna_12.text:
*I browse photos of the school, cherry blossoms, and a cat beside the gym.*

Plenty to photograph here, huh?

day1_lunch_yuna_13.text: *As I keep scrolling, I find the same cherry tree photographed at different times of day. Morning, noon, sunset, night.*

day1_lunch_yuna_14.text: You photographed the same tree four times?

day1_lunch_yuna_15.text: Its colors change at different times of day. I took these over a month.

day1_lunch_yuna_16.text:
*Each photo has a tiny timestamp. Yuna starts to move to the next one, then quickly goes back to the previous photo.*

You can skip that one. You flipped past it so fast, I don't think it was for me.

day1_lunch_riin_1.text: *I opened the door to the nurse's office. A faint smell of disinfectant.*

day1_lunch_riin_2.text: *A short, dark-purple bob. White coat, thin-framed glasses. She leans back in her chair, reading through a few pages.*

day1_lunch_riin_3.text: Oh, the nurse's office on your first day? Are you feeling sick?

day1_lunch_riin_4.text: My head hurts a bit. I didn't think I could keep sitting in class, so I came here. Could I sit for a little while?

day1_lunch_riin_6.text:
*Nurse Riin touches my forehead. Her hand is cool.*

Your hand's cool. I didn't come because of a fever, but… can I stay like this for a second?

day1_lunch_riin_7.text: No fever. A lot of students feel this way on their first day.

day1_lunch_riin_8.text: *She opens a drawer and takes out some medicine, smiling.*

day1_lunch_riin_9.text: Have you eaten? You shouldn't take medicine on an empty stomach.

day1_lunch_riin_10.text:
*She hands me an energy bar.*

Eat this first. Then take the medicine.

day1_lunch_riin_11.text: If you're sleepy, feel free to rest here for a bit.

day1_lunch_riin_12.text:
*The curtain is halfway down, and the bed sheets smell like laundry soap.*

I can smell soap. It's quieter here than in class; I think I could fall asleep straight away. I'll just rest a little.

day1_lunch_riin_13.text: *I close my eyes for a moment. The sounds outside fade until only the smell of disinfectant remains.*

day1_lunch_riin_14.text: *I wake under a blanket. In the sunlight, I see a faint pressure mark on the inside of my wrist, as if a thermometer had pressed against it.*

day1_lunch_riin_15.text: You're awake. You slept about 15 minutes.

day1_lunch_riin_16.text: Sorry, I dozed off. I lay down to rest, but I didn't think I'd actually fall asleep. It's not time for class yet, is it?

day1_lunch_riin_17.text: This room is here so you can rest. Is your head feeling any better?

day1_lunch_riin_18.text: Yes, a little. I must have fallen asleep.

day1_lunch_alone_1.text: *I climbed the stairs and opened the rooftop door. The wind hits me full on.*

day1_lunch_alone_2.text: *I eat a rice ball while looking down at the sports field.*

day1_lunch_alone_3.text: *A lens flashed once from the corner of the field.*

day1_lunch_alone_4.text: *There was no shutter sound. Only the wind from the field rose up toward me.*

day1_lunch_alone_5.text: *There are scratch marks under the railing. Old traces. When I run my fingertips over them, three short lines catch against my skin.*

day1_lunch_end.text: *Lunch is over. Time for afternoon classes.*

day1_lunch_sea_share_1.text: Trade me a sausage. I made them, but yours looks better.

day1_lunch_sea_share_2.text: So even class presidents eye other people’s food.

day1_lunch_sea_share_3.text: The class president’s on lunch break. Right now, I’m just Han Sea.

day1_lunch_sea_share_4.text: *We traded sausages. Sea slid a napkin under my lid. Only after wiping off the sauce did I realize I hadn’t had one.*

day1_lunch_riin_rest_1.text: Yes. But I can’t see the clock. What if I fall asleep again?

day1_lunch_riin_rest_2.text: I’ll wake you. Watching the clock in your sleep hardly counts as resting.

day1_lunch_riin_rest_3.text: *She moved the water to the head of the bed and drew the window curtain a little farther. The sunlight left my eyelids.*

day1_lunch_sea_menu_choice.text: *Sea tapped the empty side-dish compartment with the tips of her chopsticks.*
choices: Ask how much sugar she put in the rolled omelet
Point to the English initials scratched on the bottom of the lunchbox

day1_lunch_sea_menu_1.text: About the rolled omelet. You put quite a bit of sugar in it, right? I could taste it from the first bite.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_2.text: Two teaspoons. Any less and your blood sugar drops in the afternoon, and you start yawning.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_3.text: How do you know I yawn in the afternoon? This is my first day.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_4.text:
*Sea tightened her fingers around the water-bottle cap as she twisted it.*

You did it twice during morning homeroom, looking out the window. Class reps notice these things.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_5.text: I can't tell if you're observant or if you've only been watching me.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_6.text: You're the transfer student. I'm keeping an eye on you. Want tomorrow's side dishes less sweet?

day1_lunch_sea_menu_7.text: No, make them just like today's. They were good.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_8.text: There are two letters scratched into the corner of that lunchbox. They aren't your initials.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_9.text: *Sea instinctively cupped her palm beneath the lunchbox to cover them.*

day1_lunch_sea_menu_10.text: Someone and I shared this box last year. The scouring pad must have scratched it while I was washing up.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_11.text: Those strokes looked pretty straight for scouring-pad scratches.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_12.text: You're imagining it. Old things get marks on them.

day1_lunch_sea_menu_13.text: *Sea folded a napkin and stacked it neatly beside the lunchbox.*

day1_lunch_sea_menu_14.text: If you're finished, I'll close the lid. You'll get grease on your hands.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_choice.text: *Yuna's fingers trembled slightly over the camera's arrow buttons.*
choices: Ask about the photo she just hurriedly skipped
Point to the picture of the empty bench under the cherry tree

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_1.text: Why hide the picture you just skipped? Is it blurry?

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_2.text: The exposure was wrong. I'm embarrassed to show you a washed-out picture.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_3.text: *In the corner of the screen, I caught a glimpse of the school-gate plaque instead of a library window.*

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_4.text: It looked like you took it by the gate. Were you photographing people arriving this morning?

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_5.text: Sometimes. The shadows at the gate are longest at exactly 8 a.m.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_6.text: You even memorize the time for your photos.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_7.text: The light comes in at the same angle every day. Only the people change.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_8.text: Why is the bench under that cherry tree empty in this picture? It looks like someone was sitting there.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_9.text: *Yuna brushed her thumb across the camera screen.*

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_10.text: I took it right after they got up. There were petals piled everywhere, but that spot was bare once they stood up.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_12.text: I don't know. By the time I turned around, they'd already gone toward the stairs.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_13.text: *Yuna fitted the lens cap with a dry plastic click.*

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_14.text: Sunbae, you should go before afternoon classes start. The first-floor hallway gets crowded just before the bell.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_15.text: Thanks. Show me some more when you finish sorting them.

day1_lunch_yuna_lens_16.text: Okay. I won't delete them. I'll keep them just as they are.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_choice.text: *When I stepped off the bed, my slippers clung coldly to the linoleum tiles.*
choices: Ask about the thermometer mark on the inside of my wrist
Look at the timetable on the clipboard on her desk

day1_lunch_riin_chart_1.text: Ms. Riin, did you check my temperature again while I was asleep? It left a mark on my wrist.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_2.text: Yes. Your pulse seemed a little faster than when I felt your forehead.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_3.text: You take a pulse at the wrist, though. This looks like something metal pressed against it.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_4.text: *Ms. Riin slipped a hand into her coat pocket and tilted her head slightly.*

day1_lunch_riin_chart_5.text: My watch buckle must have brushed it. I tried to be careful. I didn't want to wake you.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_6.text: I see. I slept really well, thanks to you.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_7.text: If your head feels heavy again this afternoon, come down. No need to put up with it.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_8.text: Is that a list of today's infirmary visitors on the clipboard?

day1_lunch_riin_chart_9.text: *Ms. Riin tapped the top of the clipboard lightly with her pen.*

day1_lunch_riin_chart_10.text: Yes. You're the first one this lunchtime.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_11.text: There are eraser marks on the line above mine.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_12.text: I wrote a student number wrong this morning. Lucky I used pencil instead of pen.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_13.text: *She swept the eraser crumbs off the paper with her palm and shook them into the bin.*

day1_lunch_riin_chart_14.text: Don't take medicine on an empty stomach. At least get some milk before the cafeteria closes.

day1_lunch_riin_chart_15.text: I will. Thank you for letting me rest.

day1_lunch_alone_rail_choice.text: *Three short lines were gouged side by side into a patch of peeling paint beneath the rooftop railing.*
choices: Check the depth of the scratches with my fingernail
Look again for the lens that glinted in the corner of the field

day1_lunch_alone_rail_1.text: *I pressed my thumbnail into a groove and moved it slowly. Only the layer of gray paint over the rusty metal had been cut deeply.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_2.text: *Beside the three lines, a faint fourth stroke stopped partway through.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_3.text: Was someone counting days up here?

day1_lunch_alone_rail_4.text: *I rubbed the gray dust from my fingertip onto my trousers. It stayed in the creases of my skin.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_5.text: *I leaned over the railing and looked down at the shade beside the gym, where something had glinted earlier.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_6.text: *The end of a black camera strap slipped out of sight between the plane-tree branches.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_7.text: Photography club? There shouldn't be any reason to photograph the rooftop.

day1_lunch_alone_rail_8.text: *I crumpled the rice-ball wrapper into my pocket. The rooftop door rattled in the wind.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_9.text: *The inside of the door handle was still faintly warm when I gripped it.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_11.text: *I looked down the stairs. There was no sign of anyone, all the way to the fourth-floor hallway.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_12.text: *Distant cheers from the field drifted through the gap in the landing window.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_13.text: *I rubbed my fingers together as I went downstairs. The paint dust still felt gritty against my skin.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_14.text: *The warning bell began to ring as I turned into the third-floor hallway.*

day1_lunch_alone_rail_15.text: *Before I opened the classroom door, I noticed the empty desk diagonally behind my seat.*
